outcomeClusters.title: Work
outcomes: State the full definition of work.
Describe the relationship between work and direction.
Calculate work done with an angle of 0°, 180°, or 90°.

outcomeClusters.title: Energy Definitions & Types
outcomes: Define total energy.
Define mechanical energy.
Identify potential energy and kinetic energy as types of mechanical energies.
Identify the total mechanical energy in a situation given the description.
Calculate the total mechanical energy of a system.

outcomeClusters.title: Gravitational Potential Energy
outcomes: Identify gravitational potential energy in a situation given an appropriate reference point.
Define gravitational potential energy.
Calculate gravitational potential energy.

outcomeClusters.title: Kinetic Energy
outcomes: Identify whether an object possesses kinetic energy in a situation.
Define kinetic energy.
Calculate kinetic energy.

outcomeClusters.title: Conservation of Energy
outcomes: Define open and closed systems for everyday situations.
Apply conservation of energy to isolated systems to be able to identify the relative amount of mechanical energy at each point in the system.
State what types of energy transformation are occurring in a given situation.
State when conservation of mechanical energy does not apply.
Calculate/describe the changes in potential, kinetic, or spring energies in an isolated system with changes in the others.

outcomeClusters.title: Spring Potential Energy
outcomes: Define spring potential energy.
Calculate spring potential energy from a description of a situation.

outcomeClusters.title: Work-Energy Theorem
outcomes: Apply the work-energy theorem to a given situation (i.e., identify that an increase in kinetic energy means positive work is applied).
Calculate or describe the amount of energy in the system given the amount of work done or vice versa.
